text: Hello, this is the Windows technical department. We are receiving error reports from your computer showing that it has been infected with a dangerous virus.
tell: Software companies do not monitor your PC and phone you about infections.

text: Hi, I'm calling from your internet provider. Your router's IP address has been used by hackers, and your connection will be suspended unless we secure your network today.
tell: Unsolicited 'your IP was hacked' calls are a pretext to get remote access to your device.

text: Thank you for calling the number on the security warning on your screen. Do not turn off or restart the computer, or you could lose all your files permanently.
tell: Browser pop-ups with phone numbers are fake; restarting is safe and closes the scare page.

text: I am a certified Microsoft technician and your computer licence ID is linked to our server. I can prove the infection is real by showing you the errors in the event viewer.
tell: Event Viewer always shows harmless warnings; showing them as 'proof' is a scripted trick.

text: Our security team has traced foreign hackers accessing your online banking from this device. We work together with your bank's fraud department on cases like yours.
tell: Tech companies do not run joint fraud investigations with your bank about your personal device.

text: Look at all the red and yellow warnings on this screen, every one of those is an active threat. I have seen hundreds of these and yours is one of the worst I've seen.
tell: Normal system logs dressed up as an emergency to justify an expensive 'fix'.

text: Don't let anybody else use the computer or check email until I finish, because any activity will alert the hackers that we are onto them.
tell: Keeps family from seeing the remote session and noticing what the 'technician' is doing.

text: Please don't call your bank or your children about this right now. The hackers may be listening through your phone, and I will explain everything to them afterwards.
tell: Blocking calls to the bank and family is isolation, not security.

text: Keep the computer switched on and stay close to it. If you hang up, the remote session is locked and the hackers will have full control of your device.
tell: Hanging up and disconnecting the internet is the right action; the threat is invented to stop it.

text: Your files are being encrypted as we speak. If we don't install the protection in the next few minutes, your photos and documents will be lost forever.
tell: Fake ransomware countdown to force installation of remote-access software.

text: The hackers are trying to transfer money out of your account right now. We have to lock down your banking before they finish, so please act quickly.
tell: Pivot from computer problem to bank account is where tech support scams take money.

text: Your warranty support expires today, and after that each repair costs more than a thousand dollars. It is much cheaper to renew the protection plan now.
tell: A same-day expiring 'protection plan' sold on an unsolicited call.

text: Go to the website I will spell out and download the support tool, then read me the nine digit access code so I can connect to your computer.
tell: The access code hands a stranger full control of your computer, including your banking sessions.

text: The protection plan is two hundred ninety-nine dollars for three years. Log into your bank on the screen so I can process the payment for you.
tell: Logging into your bank while a stranger controls the screen lets them move money and fake the balance.

text: I accidentally refunded you ten thousand instead of one hundred. You need to send back the difference, so please go to the store and buy gift cards for that amount.
tell: The 'overpayment' is your own money moved between your accounts; gift cards are the untraceable cash-out.
